summary:
The Black Caiman (*Melanosuchus niger*) is the largest predator of the Amazon Basin — a sleek, dark giant that once glided silently through the river systems of Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and beyond. Reaching lengths of up to six meters, these ancient reptiles shaped their ecosystems as apex predators, keeping rivers in balance across millions of acres of floodplain forest.

For much of the 20th century, the Black Caiman was hunted relentlessly for its prized skin, pushing populations to the edge of collapse. Once among the most endangered crocodilians on Earth, decades of legal protection have allowed this species to recover — a rare and hopeful story of return from the brink.
